summary: The note argues that national cyber defense depends on public-private partnerships (PPPs), built on information sharing, joint innovation and collaborative incident response. It cites examples such as the Cyber Threat Alliance, the UK's CiSP, Cyber NYC and NATO's Cyber Coalition exercises. It also covers proposed corporate cybersecurity liaisons, privacy and interest-balancing challenges, the EU Cyber Resilience Act, and building a culture of cyber readiness.
one_line: Public-private partnerships in cyber defense rely on information sharing, joint innovation and joint incident response, while balancing corporate, security and privacy interests.
key_facts: A ransomware attack on October 12, 2023 targeted several multinational corporations and public institutions and paralyzed critical services for hours.
President Kathleen Hale of the United States said on November 5, 2023: "Cyber defense is a shared responsibility."
PPP frameworks in cybersecurity typically have three components: information sharing, joint innovation, and collaborative incident response.

The Cyber Threat Alliance (CTA), started in late 2023, is an initiative by several tech corporations with the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to enable real-time exchange of data on cyber threats and vulnerabilities.
The United Kingdom established the Cyber Security Information Sharing Partnership (CiSP) as part of its national cybersecurity strategy.
Michael Anderson, CEO of CyberGuard Tech, said on February 10, 2024 that joining forces with national labs and research universities makes defense capability 'squared'.
Cyber NYC, a public-private partnership launched in autumn 2023 in New York City, aims to make the city a global hub for cyber innovation.
NATO member states take part in coordinated cyber defense exercises like 'Cyber Coalition', which nations are looking to as a model for civilian cyber crisis management.
Cybersecurity liaison roles within corporations are proposed as designated contacts for government agencies to streamline real-time communication.
Dr. Emily Cho, a cybersecurity policy expert, led a workshop on liaisons at the International Cybersecurity Forum (FIC) on March 16, 2024.

The European Union introduced the Cyber Resilience Act on September 20, 2023, setting rules for the security of digital products and services and mechanisms for information exchange between member states and businesses.

Cybersecurity Awareness Month, observed in October since 2004, took a more participatory approach in 2023, with workshops for small businesses and drills involving large corporations and government agencies.
Key challenges include balancing corporate interests, national security concerns and individual privacy rights.
